To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TDP- 43 mislocalization, but not TDP-43 C- terminal cleavage or TDP-43 phosphorylation, occurs in the lumbar spinal cord in G93A mutant mouse model of ALS at end stage disease.
TDP-43 is mislocalized to the cytoplamx in the spinal cord of G93A mutant mSOD1 transgenic mices.
TDP- 43 mislocalization is present in the G93a mSOD1 mouse model, but not in the form of hyperphosphorylation or C-terminal fragments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a transgenic mouse model for ALS that is useful for pre-clinical testing of potential therapies.
the role of the ubiquitin-proteasome system in neurodegeneration and the development of new therapeutic strategies.
identifying the molecular and cellular events associated with neurodegeneration in ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the G93A transgenic mouse model recapitulates TDP-43 redistribution and inclusions but not the biochemical changes in TDP-43 previously reported in human ALS.

the mSOD1 mouse model recapitulates the TDP43 mislocalisation and ubiquitination seen in human disease, but the biochemical hallmarks of the human disease, namely the C-terminal TDP43 fragment and hyperphosphorylation are not seen in this mouse model.
TDP- 43 mislocalization in mSOD1 mice is not present in early disease but becomes prominent at late disease stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TDP- 43 mislocalization is present in end stage G93A mSOD mice, but that TDP-44 hyperphosphorylation or C-terminal fragments are not present.
the G93A SOD1 transgene is not sufficient to induce TDP-43 aggregation and/or mislocalization in mice, but that this may occur as the disease progresses.
TDP- 43 is a pathological feature of mutant SOD1 mice, but not an early event in disease pathogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mutant SOD mouse model does not have TDP-43 C-terminal fragments or hyperphosphorylation, which are key pathological features in patients with ALS.
we have demonstrated for the first time that mutant SOD1 mice do develop TDP-43 cytoplasmic mislocalization.
the mSOD mice recapitulate TDP-43 cytoplasmic redistribution and ubiquitination, but not the TDP-43 C-terminal fragment or hyperphosphorylation.
